A single, isolated set of gothic wizardry robes: a floor-length ceremonial garment with a high, protective cowl rising like a shadowed arch around the head opening. The fabric reads as heavy midnight velvet layered over matte charcoal linen, threaded with faint, silvery filaments that resemble loom-warp lines when caught by light. Across the chest and down the sleeves, intricate embroidered sigils form repeating textile motifs—spools, shuttle-shapes, and interlaced knots—suggesting warding patterns woven into the seams. The silhouette is well framed and centered, with broad shoulders, long draping sleeves, and a structured mantle that falls in clean, symmetrical folds. Subtle metallic clasps at the throat mimic tiny loom bars, and the hem is weighted with narrow leaded trim to keep the robe’s protective geometry precise.
